programme_or_channel: Industrial park and economic zone canteens (national)
meals_per_year_basis: our calculation: 4.15 million x 300 meal days; upper bound
rules: Union floor VND 20,000 (Hai Phong); employer-organised meals tax exempt; cash allowance tax-free to VND 1.2 million per month from 1 Jul 2026 (Decree 253/2026)
notes: Some firms pay cash instead of meals; workers outside parks not counted. Version 0.4: union shift-meal floors (VGCL Conclusion 03, 2022) are VND 25,000 when a caterer is hired and VND 20,000 when the firm cooks itself in regions I and II (VND 22,000 and 18,000 in regions III and IV); each meal must include a protein food group (AIB-43).

rules: 2 to 3 main dishes, 1 vegetable dish, soup, dessert; 62% of unionised firms use kitchens, caterers, vouchers or cash
notes: Toyota Boshoku 33,000; Toyoda Gosei 30,000; Sumiden 35,000. Version 0.4: 2026 average about VND 31,000 (east) and 27,000 (west), some firms VND 17,000; union negotiations raised firms from 20,000 to 22,000, 22,000 to 28,000 and 24,000 to 26,500 (UPL-34).

programme_or_channel: Northern garment firm and Ho Guom group canteens
rules: Union-negotiated; 2016 minimum VND 15,000; 2022 recommendation 18,000 to 20,000; proposals of 25,000 to 29,000
notes: Duc Giang (over 1,000 workers), Hung Yen Garment (1,692 staff), Ho Guom group (about 130 meals a day; VND 17,000 in 2024, 20,000 in 2025, 25,000 in 2026)

rules: Food 60% to 80% of meal value; informal commissions VND 500 to 1,000 per meal to purchasing staff
notes: About USD 2 bn, 7% CAGR; Vietnam EOC 120,000 meals a day; Hoang Kim 50,000; Vinastory 38,000; Dussmann and Thao Ha about 30,000 each. Version 0.4: Haseca reports more than 200,000 meals a day from more than 120 kitchens in five tiers of VND 18,000 to 45,000 (company claim, AIB-36); caterers' published menus lead with pork 33%, fish 26% and chicken 13% of protein dishes, tofu 9%, and name no textured soy (UPL-27; UPL-32).

programme_or_channel: Hanoi primary school lunch subsidy (ban tru)
meals_per_year_basis: our calculation: VND 3,063 bn / VND 20,000 to 30,000 = about 100 to 150 million pupil meals (midpoint shown)
rules: Subsidy VND 20,000 per day, VND 30,000 in mountainous and island areas; minimum meal VND 30,000; up to 9 months; parents pay the difference; 703 schools (90.4%) provide ban tru
notes: Budget about VND 3,063 billion; 707,727 public and 60,273 private pupils. Version 0.4: for 2026 to 2027 see INS-017 (VND 40,000 a meal, city VND 28,000).

rules: Lunch ceiling VND 35,000 to 50,000; breakfast 20,000 to 25,000; preschool 35,000 to 40,000; covers labour, equipment, transport, QA
notes: Proposal of 23 Sep 2026

rules: Minimum VND 30,000 in major cities; international schools VND 120,000 to 140,000 a day for three meals
notes: About 26,000 public schools; 15.5 million primary and lower secondary pupils per CHN-31

programme_or_channel: School meals, national rules after 2026 pork case
rules: Dispatch 64/CD-TTg: public, transparent procurement not solely on lowest price; supplier food-safety capability and traceability; age-appropriate balanced menus
notes: About 300 t ASF pork reached 26 Hanoi public schools and private kindergartens in April 2026. Version 0.4: supplier documents and daily disclosure are now set by Directive 33/CT-TTg (INS-016).

meals_per_year_basis: our calculation: 417,708 pupils x about 198 lunch days (9 months x 22 days)
rules: Lunch support for primary and lower-secondary pupils in land-border communes: VND 450,000 a month plus 8 kg of rice for up to 9 months; schools receive VND 2,369,000 a month per 45 pupils eating together; more than VND 2,000 billion and 30,000 t of rice a year
notes: Version 0.4: amounts and pupil numbers added (price per meal is lunch money for non-rice food per school day, our calculation). An observed Decree 339 lunch at Muong Nhe spent 79 to 98% of its non-rice money on pork (91 to 98% on pork and tofu together) (107 to 179 g raw a pupil); no upland lunch in the sample was animal-free.

rules: Decision 1340/QD-TTg (8 Jul 2016): 100% of preschool and primary children in poor districts, 70% elsewhere by 2020; animal protein over 40% of total protein; funding from enterprises, families and local budgets
notes: Precedent for state-driven protein food demand. Version 0.4: the Decision 1340 targets ended in 2020; it is not a current school-protein rule. Current guidance is Decision 3958/QĐ-BYT (INS-014), which sets no animal share. The dairy strategy (Decision 309/QĐ-TTg, 2026) emphasises school meals with fresh milk only (APR-11).

people_served_unit: over 90% of preschool and primary children
rules: State 30% (50% disadvantaged), supplier 23%, parents about 47%; milk made entirely in Vietnam; public tender won by Vinamilk
notes: Contract over VND 3,828 billion

meals_per_year_basis: tender quantity: about 81,842 rice meals and 20,461 porridge meals a year (Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Ho Chi Minh City)
rules: At least 1,800 kcal (rice) or 1,200 kcal (porridge) and 60 g of protein a day; per meal at least 60 g of meat, fish or poultry, or at least 120 g of tofu as a full replacement; seafood at most one third of a day's menu; sealed labelled containers; at least three sample menus with photos (meat, seafood and tofu versions)
notes: Version 0.4: replaces the open placeholder. 120 g of tofu gives about 13.1 g of protein against 11.4 g for 60 g of meat (our calculation). Patient meal budgets were not in the page; one tender only.

rules: Circular 96/2025/TT-BQP (25 August 2025): basic infantry food allowance VND 72,000 (USD 2.77) per person per day; replaces Circular 168/2021/TT-BQP (earlier rate not in this source); ration composition and procurement not retrieved
notes: Version 0.4: replaces the open placeholder; the circular text was not found, only the allowance.

rules: MOH guidance of 25 Dec 2025 for general, boarding and semi-boarding schools (preschools excluded): protein 13 to 20% of energy; lunch 30 to 40% of daily energy; animal protein on at least 4 to 5 days a week alternating with plant protein (legumes, tofu) at least twice a week; fish or seafood 2 to 3 times a week; no animal share of protein; limit processed meat and sausages; food table lists tofu, soybeans and soy milk but no textured soy or analogue; no sanction
notes: Version 0.4: added. Audited menus meet the twice-weekly plant rule in only 9 of 48 school-weeks and fill it with tofu beside meat; plant protein appears on 15.1% of 239 lunch days (PMR-10; PMR-31).

rules: Prime Minister, 1 June 2026: MOET circular on school nutrition education and bán trú meal organisation (due 2026); scale up the school meal model (ongoing); MOET digital tools to build balanced menus (2027 to 2028); MOF to revise Circular 14/2007 on school health funding (2026); 100% of schools serving meals meet food-safety conditions by 2030 (93.1% in 2026); funding may include enterprises and international aid
notes: Version 0.4: added. The text names no company, menu count or milk; press reports of 400 menus and a daily milk carton come from coverage, not the decision (AFN-45). This is the rule window for school menus.

rules: Prime Minister, 14 Aug 2026: provinces list and evaluate all suppliers by September 2026; check legal status, food-safety certificates and food quality; daily public disclosure of caterer, ingredients, purchase invoices, menus and tray photos; MOET to finish meal-organisation rules in Q4 2026; restricts no food type
notes: Version 0.4: added. Ho Chi Minh City Document 9632 implements it and bars a supplier from serving more schools than its capacity. Read through a fetch summary.

programme_or_channel: Hanoi public primary school lunch, 2026 to 2027 (Resolution 84/2026/NQ-HĐND)
rules: VND 40,000 per pupil per meal (lunch and snack): city pays VND 28,000, parents VND 12,000; care fee VND 235,000 a month; ward evaluation councils list capable suppliers and assign caterers, food, milk and water suppliers school by school; caterer writes the menu and the principal co-signs
notes: Version 0.4: added. One Bo De ward notice covers 14 public schools; one caterer wrote near-identical menus for three schools.

programme_or_channel: Ho Chi Minh City primary school lunch
rules: School kitchen or a caterer approved by the principal; schools ask for quotes with a price plan and capability dossier, and the commune appraises the chosen supplier
notes: Version 0.4: added.

programme_or_channel: Hai Phong school meal tender (Chu Van An Primary)
meals_per_year_basis: our calculation: about 45,100 meals a month x 9 months
rules: Price at the regulated norm; bidders compete on the extra portion value they add; business registration, food-safety certificate, revenue of at least VND 3 billion, catering contracts with at least 3 schools or industrial zones, certified food suppliers; ready-processed foods only with clear origin, compliant packaging and a use-by date; caterer writes a 20-day menu (rice, main protein dish, vegetable, soup, dessert and a milk or cake snack)
notes: Version 0.4: added. Shows the documents a caterer, and so an ingredient supplier, must hold.

rules: VND 936,000 a month plus 15 kg of rice; VND 360,000 more a month if housing is self-arranged; up to 9 months a year; covers two or three meals a day for boarders in ethnic minority and mountain areas; in force 1 May 2025
notes: Version 0.4: added. Per school day: VND 46,800 over 20 days or about VND 40,700 to 42,500 over 22 to 23 days (our calculation). Schools state boarding meal costs of VND 17,000 to 27,500 a meal (UPL-23; UPL-17).

programme_or_channel: New boarding schools including land-border communes (Decree 188/2026/ND-CP)
rules: Full boarder VND 1,170,000 a month plus 15 kg of rice; midday boarder VND 450,000 plus 8 kg; up to 9 months; signed 27 May 2026, in force 15 July 2026
notes: Version 0.4: added. Per day: about VND 45,000 over 26 days or 53,200 over 22 days (our calculation). Upland boarding lunches and dinners carried meat, fish or egg in 240 of 242 meals (UPL-01; UPL-09).

rules: Charity-funded lunch at preschool and primary satellite sites: VND 8,000 a lunch (VND 1,144,000 for 143 pupils); 34 g pork and 82 g tofu, or 1.7 duck eggs, a pupil
notes: Version 0.4: added.

programme_or_channel: Hope Foundation and De Heus Vietnam school meal top-up
rules: A feed company funding breakfasts and an extra dish at three boarding schools (Son La, Thanh Hoa, Nghe An): about VND 10,000 more a meal; VND 1.2 billion since 1 October 2024
notes: Version 0.4: added.

programme_or_channel: School menu software standard (MOET, Ajinomoto Vietnam and NIN)
price_per_meal_vnd: asks each school for its lunch fee
rules: Balanced-menu software and menu bank (120+ menus, 360+ dishes behind a school login); nutrition sheets print a standard of animal protein at least 48% of protein per lunch; not enforced (9 of 25 published days fall below it)
notes: Version 0.4: added. A software default, not law: national guidance (INS-014) sets no animal share. MOET is asked to update the software to Decision 3958.
